clue.text: Very tiny messy sample behind a bag for cosmetics

indicators.note: behind places the jumbled tiny and the sample after the letter a
something messy is jumbled up, so the letters of tiny are rearranged

parts.note: a case is an instance or sample of something

explanation.surface: Someone notes a very small, untidy specimen lying behind a cosmetics bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' is the anagram signal on the word tiny; 'behind a' places that jumble and the sample after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small case carried by a woman to hold make-up and toiletries is exactly this kind of bag.

clue.text: Bottom lifted of disgusting mask

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom letter of the word for disgusting is raised higher up the word

parts.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: Something revolting sits under a mask that has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom lifted' moves the final E of VILE up two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil covers the face, so it serves as a mask or disguise.

clue.text: Well-groomed bovine

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle, an ox or cow

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy, and neat is also an archaic noun for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.

clue.text: Picture everything

definitions.meaning: a film: the 1997 British comedy about Sheffield strippers
the whole lot, a British idiom

explanation.surface: Imagine it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for the whole lot and the title of a popular 1997 British film about amateur strippers.

clue.text: Fat like a fish?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, resembling a chub, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Is a fat person rather fishlike?
explanation.definitionFit: Plump people are called this; the chub is also a river fish, so the word can jokingly mean chub-like.

clue.text: Charge by day, universal charge

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A billing note: a daily fee plus a flat fee for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge something fully, with liquid or electricity, is to fill it completely, which is soaking it through.

clue.text: Being partial to war, essentially?

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who is, at heart, fond of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of war is a divine being, and the surface's fondness for war hints at him.

clue.text: One of four players getting 0 — 0* runs

parts.note: the figure 0 is drawn as a ring
the figure 0 is also the letter O
the symbol * is a star
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: one of four batsmen made a duck and was not out on nought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring an asterisk marks a not-out score, so '0*' looks like a scorecard entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The drummer was one of the four musicians who made up the Beatles.

clue.text: Cryptically in top fielding position?

parts.note: the word point, made silly, that is jumbled, gives these two words

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is placed in a top, cryptically clever spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'silly' is an anagram signal applied to POINT, which gives IN TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a close catching position near the batsman on the off side.

clue.text: Lacking in a river, about two pints? That's no river!

indicators.note: that's no river means the abbreviation for river is then removed
about means the river phrase goes round the measure

parts.note: taken as written
the Dee is a river in Britain
a quart is two pints
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river measurement falls short: about a quart, and then not a river at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Britain; 'That's no river' then removes the R from the assembled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inadequate means insufficient, falling short, which is wanting or deficient.

clue.text: A love for dye

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so nil

explanation.surface: Giving up a love for a colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is indigo, a blue dye from a West Indian plant.

clue.text: Something bitter I knocked up in soup that's hot

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the soup

parts.note: chowder is a thick soup

indicators.note: in a down entry, knocked up means the word is turned upwards and read backwards

parts.note: a pill is something bitter to swallow

explanation.surface: A bitter ingredient knocked together into a hot soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'knocked up' turns the bitter pill upwards; chowder is a thick, often seafood, soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground dried peppers make a spice that is fiery to the taste, something hot.

clue.text: Place to break your men, complex maths

indicators.note: to break means the place word goes inside, splitting the other letters
complex means the letters of your men are tangled and rearranged

parts.note: a berth is a place, a bunk or mooring

explanation.surface: An instruction to station your troops among them, followed by a tricky sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' turns YOUR MEN into NUMEORY, broken by BERTH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of mathematics studying integers and their properties, such as primes.

clue.text: Higher up, sides of garments tight — like these?

definitions.text: Higher up, sides of garments tight — like these?

indicators.note: tight in the sense of drunk signals that the letters are muddled
sides of means the outer letters of garments are taken

explanation.surface: Trousers worn low, describing how they sit tight on the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' scrambles HIGHER UP plus GS, the outside letters of garments.
explanation.definitionFit: These low-waisted trousers cling to the hips, so their sides are tight around the body.

clue.text: Clean broadcast stank when screened

indicators.note: screened means hidden from view by the outer word, so it goes inside

parts.note: seeds broadcast by hand are sown
ponged is British slang for stank

explanation.surface: A TV programme on cleaning that smelled bad when shown.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe a surface over with a wet sponge is to wash it.

clue.text: Monkey in the style of antelope

parts.note: a mischievous child, an imp, is called a little monkey
a la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: A monkey dressed up as a horned grazer.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African antelope.

clue.text: Getting toilet seat hollowed out, newly sharpened implement

indicators.note: hollowed out means seat loses its middle, leaving its outer letters
newly suggests the letters are made over in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bathroom refit: a new toilet with a gutted seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges TOILET with ST, the shell left of seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a narrow pointed blade.

clue.text: Clever getting 50% off bran in breakfast

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the breakfast word

parts.note: cereal is a typical breakfast

indicators.note: half the word bran is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A smart shopper getting half-price bran for the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means intellectual, of the brain, so brainy or intelligent.

clue.text: Gatecrashing house good for headbanger?

indicators.note: gatecrashing means one letter barges into the royal house name

parts.note: Hanover is a royal house of Britain

explanation.surface: An uninvited guest at a party for heavy-metal fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning-after condition brings a pounding head, so the question mark makes it a whimsical headbanger.

clue.text: Initially, cultivation time's cut to press fruit

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of cultivation
cut to means the time letter cuts into the press word

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Farming time is reduced so the fruit can be pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large citrus fruit, like a lemon with thick rind.

clue.text: Harden hearts of those lasses, pacifist pussycats

indicators.note: hearts of means the central letters of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A call for gentle girls and their pet cats to toughen up.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are O, SS, IF and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is to turn into bone, hence to become rigid or set in one's ways.

clue.text: Gas reported swirling on planet, ultimately a distant hurricane

indicators.note: swirling gas suggests the letters are spun into a new order
ultimately means the last letter of planet

explanation.surface: News of swirling gas on a planet, a storm far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges GAS REPORTED into GREATREDSPO; T ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter's famous feature is a giant storm system, a long-lived anticyclone far from Earth.

clue.text: Something in the mouth, new smoke rings

indicators.note: rings means the smoke word surrounds the new letter

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A fresh cigarette in the mouth blows smoke rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, found in the mouth.

clue.text: A ropy bird?

definitions.meaning: jocular: a thing made of rope, a tie in a line
a wading bird of the sandpiper family

explanation.surface: Is this bird a bit stringy?
explanation.definitionFit: A tie made in rope is ropy by nature, and the same word names a small wading bird.

clue.text: Love god seen at horny beast's rear?

indicators.note: the rear of the beast's name is kept and its front dropped

parts.note: a rhinoceros is a beast with a horn

explanation.surface: A love god spotted at the back end of a horned animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the tail end of RHINOCEROS is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Daughter, caught between showers east of Bangladeshi capital, minds going abroad?

indicators.note: in an across entry east of puts what follows to the right
capital means the first letter of Bangladeshi
caught between places the daughter letter between the two lots of rain

parts.note: showers are rain
showers plural gives rain a second time

explanation.surface: A daughter caught in monsoon downpours in Dhaka, deciding to emigrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The emigration of highly educated people is the loss of clever minds overseas.

clue.text: Writing ultimately by issue number

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of writing

explanation.surface: Writing a magazine issue, in the end, by its number.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number is a piece performed, such as a tune with words.

clue.text: Always odd bits of work in trouble for author

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the trouble word

parts.note: a plight is a trouble or predicament
ay is a poetic word for always

indicators.note: odd bits means the first and third letters of work

explanation.walkthrough: AY is an old poetic word for always, not the more familiar 'aye' meaning yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a writer of plays, a kind of author.
